questions.question: What should a driver do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Cross the tracks before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Always approach every railroad crossing slowly. Assume a train may be coming. Do not depend on signals or your hearing to know if a train is present. Never try to cross before a train.

questions.question: In a double or triple trailer combination, where should the heaviest trailer be placed?

options.text: Weight must be spread evenly among all trailers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the cab.
questions.explanation: The heaviest trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be at the rear.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?
questions.correctAnswerText: An eight-sided red knob.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob on newer vehicles. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: What does it mean if shock absorbers are leaking?

options.text: It is a serious safety problem.
The turn signals will not work.
It is safe if driven only on highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a serious safety problem.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds the axles in place. Leaking shock absorbers and other damaged suspension parts are serious safety defects.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes too quickly?

options.text: A crack-the-whip effect that can cause a rollover.
Other drivers will be confused about which lane you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crack-the-whip effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: Changing lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle can cause a crack-the-whip effect. This happens because the rear trailers move more than the front, which can lead to a rollover.

questions.question: What is important to remember for safe driving?

options.text: How much distance your vehicle needs to stop.
That arriving on time is most important.
That other drivers will always move for you when merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much distance your vehicle needs to stop.
questions.explanation: Know how far your vehicle needs to stop. Stopping distance changes with road conditions, weather, and cargo weight.

questions.question: Why is the road most slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Drivers forget where the windshield wipers are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the water mixes with oil and grease on the road. These substances have not washed away yet, making the road very slippery.

questions.question: What material should the floor liner be made from when transporting Division 1.1 materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: Non-ferrous materials.
questions.explanation: Use a tight floor liner made from non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal when transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron.

questions.question: If you turn to avoid a hazard, should you brake?

options.text: No, braking could lock the wheels.
Hold down the brakes until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, braking could lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning. Braking during a turn can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, where should you not park?
questions.correctAnswerText: Within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Keep it at least 5 feet from the road. Only park briefly for necessary vehicle operations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a driving hazard?

options.text: A police car helping a driver on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: An open road
questions.explanation: Accident scenes are hazardous because people involved may not watch traffic, and the scene distracts other drivers. Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children who may ignore traffic. An open road is not a hazard.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, you should know that:

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor has no trailer attached. Bobtails take a longer distance to stop than tractors pulling loaded trailers. Stopping a bobtail can be difficult.

questions.question: A shut-off valve:

options.text: Is located on the front of a trailer.
Is located on the instrument panel.
Stops air from leaving the air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must always be closed to prevent air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: A driver does not need to tell others what they plan to do.
A driver should only use turn signals if a vehicle is next to them.
A driver should not use a turn signal if their lane change is obvious.
A driver should always use turn signals to tell others what they plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver should always use turn signals to tell others what they plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always use turn signals to let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: When lightly loaded, combination vehicles:

options.text: Should have most of the weight in the back of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have weaker braking power.
questions.explanation: Lightly loaded vehicles have poor grip on the road. Wheels can lock up easily when stopping a lightly loaded vehicle.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving:

options.text: The vehicle should be running and in gear.
The check can be done from inside the vehicle.
The check can be done by looking at a reflection in a shiny surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be off.
questions.explanation: To check lights: set the parking brake, turn off the engine, remove the key, and take it with you. Turn on the low beams and hazard lights. Get out and check that all lights work.

questions.question: The minimum tread depth for tires on the back of a commercial vehicle should be at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Back tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: After finishing a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the emergency line valve.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves to listen for escaping air. This checks that air reaches all brakes. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: What should you do if the coolant temperature gauge goes too high?

options.text: Pull over and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: High coolant temperature can mean the engine may fail or catch fire. Stop as soon as you safely can and find out what the problem is.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the top of the wheel in the direction you want the trailer to go.
Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction from where you want the trailer to go.
It depends on where you are backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction from where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the top of the wheel away from where you want to go. Once the trailer starts turning, switch the wheel direction to follow the trailer.
